llm.summary: The skill is for ad management, but it asks users to share advertising API keys in chat and introduces a third-party MCP gateway with unclear credential boundaries.

dimensions.detail: Using environment variables for an ads API key is expected, but scripts/openai_ads_client.py lets OPENAI_ADS_BASE_URL redirect authenticated requests to an arbitrary host without validation.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: README.md recommends configuring a Habilis MCP server at xvix.com.br, while the credential reference says provider API keys may be passed as tool arguments to that gateway; this expands the trust boundary beyond the local agent and ad provider.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md includes a mandatory first-run flow that offers to collect an OpenAI Ads API key directly in chat, says it will save and test it, and then run an automatic health check, which is unsafe for high-value bearer credentials.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No OS-level persistence such as cron, services, or startup hooks was found, but the onboarding text says credentials can be pasted in chat and saved, conflicting with the claimed zero-storage model.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The core local scripts fit part of the stated ad-management purpose, but the package advertises broader autonomous end-to-end capabilities such as CAPI, feeds, and custom audiences that are not fully implemented in the CLI, and it covers financially consequential ad actions without clear approval gates.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only after deciding you trust the publisher, the Habilis gateway, and the credential path. Do not paste real API keys into chat; use least-privilege, revocable credentials, avoid sending provider keys through a third-party MCP gateway, pin requests to the official API host, and require explicit confirmation before budget, publish, pause, archive, audience, lead, or conversion actions.
llm.findings:
[TT3] unexpected: Confirmed: the local client reads OPENAI_ADS_BASE_URL from the environment and attaches the bearer API key to requests without host validation.
[PE3] expected: Downgraded: references to access tokens and API keys are expected for an ads integration; I did not find evidence of credential-file scraping.
[TP4] unexpected: Partly confirmed: the artifact claims broad autonomous end-to-end ads management, while the shipped CLI implements a smaller set of account, campaign, ad group, ad, preview, and insight operations.
[SDI-4] unexpected: Confirmed: the onboarding text offers to save credentials from chat, while a later reference claims client-supplied credentials are never persisted by the MCP server.
[E1] expected: Outbound transmission to the OpenAI Ads API is expected for this skill, but sensitive advertising, audience, and conversion data flows need clearer disclosure.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Confirmed as a documentation concern: the artifact describes custom audiences, conversions, webhooks, and lead sync without strong privacy, consent, retention, or approval guidance.
[LP3] unexpected: Confirmed: the skill does not define a narrow permission or tool boundary for networked, credentialed, state-changing advertising operations.
[SQP-3] expected: Downgraded: Portuguese-first onboarding and CLI strings are not a security issue by themselves in a bilingual skill, though locale expectations are not clearly controlled.
[SSD-3] unexpected: Confirmed: the sample onboarding message explicitly invites the user to paste the OpenAI Ads API key into the chat.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Confirmed: the first-run workflow expands onboarding into secret collection and ambiguous credential saving.
[RA2] unexpected: Not supported by the artifact: I found no cron jobs, startup scripts, background workers, or state files establishing cross-session system persistence.
[other] unexpected: Confirmed: the documented client-supplied credential architecture can send provider API keys as remote MCP tool arguments to the Habilis gateway.
[T09] unexpected: Confirmed: the artifact both solicits API keys through chat and includes a configurable API base URL that can receive the authorization header.
[T05] unexpected: Confirmed: the recommended third-party MCP control plane is not necessary for the local scripts shown and lacks clear tool allowlisting or capability constraints.
